best_plan.name: p2
best_plan.rationale: p2 is the best cost-quality trade-off: it keeps the plan structure minimal, uses an exact filter on idx to isolate taken_3 reviews, and classifies each review directly into positive or negative with one semantic map. It achieved much better quality than p1 while keeping cost and latency nearly the same, whereas p3 only improved quality from 0.919 to 1.0 at roughly 4.7x higher cost and about 2.8x higher latency.

cost_model_explanation: The fitted cost model showed that sem_map dominates both dollar cost and latency, while filter, groupby, and project are effectively free. Observations also showed GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE was far cheaper and faster than GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH for the same operator shape, so the model favored plans that preserved a single sem_map and avoided extra semantic steps.

plan_codes.p1:
pipeline = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name, "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
pipeline.filter(lambda row: str(row["idx"]).strip().lower() == "taken_3")
pipeline.sem_map(
    [{"name": "sentiment", "type": str, "description": "Classify the review text sentiment toward the movie as exactly one of: positive, negative, or neutral."}],
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE,
    depends_on=["reviewText"]
)
pipeline.filter(lambda row: str(row["sentiment"]).strip().lower() in {"positive", "negative"})
pipeline.groupby(group_by_fields=["sentiment"], agg_funcs=["count"], agg_fields=["sentiment"])
pipeline.project(["sentiment", "count(sentiment)"])
pipeline
